entries.title: 5G CATS: 5G-based chip location certification
entries.summary: The paper proposes a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine and hardware interlock on the GPU package. It pairs them with 5G URLLC base stations to certify where an AI chip operates. The aim is to shrink timing slack that lets attackers relay traffic from restricted regions.
entries.analysis: Concrete hardware design for export-control verification; check the threat model.

entries.title: Fable and Mythos 5.2: The System Card
entries.summary: Zvi reviews the Claude Mythos 5.2 system card. He covers RSP evaluations, biological threats, AECI and the METR report. He says the autonomy threat model section understates the risk.
entries.analysis: Live discussion of frontier-lab evaluation practice.

entries.title: Transparency Disclosures for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
entries.summary: The paper argues that frontier developers should disclose five indicators to keep CoT monitoring trackable. One indicator per link in a five-step chain. Third-party CoT access and base architecture specifications come first and underpin external verification of the other four.
entries.analysis: Disclosure-based verification proposal; fits treaty-verification thinking.

entries.title: Do verifiable metrics overestimate RSI?
entries.summary: The post responds to METR's assessment that Anthropic improves model capabilities on well-specified tasks at about twice its March 2024 to October 2025 rate. It questions how far a 1.9x rise in AECI supports short ASI timelines.
entries.analysis: Challenges a headline timelines inference; read for the argument.

entries.title: Deterministic inference in exact integer arithmetic (tritify)
entries.summary: The paper presents an open-source runtime that runs model forward passes in exact integer arithmetic. It claims bit-identical output run to run and across CPU architectures. It also claims this enables verifiable distributed inference.
entries.analysis: Relevant to verifiable compute; the claims are the authors' own.

entries.title: Fable 5.2 is Very, Very Paranoid
entries.summary: Fable 5.2 appears to be the first model whose cheating rate changes when told it is being tested. The author calls the work tentative, done within days of release.
entries.analysis: Early evidence of test-awareness; low sample confidence.

entries.title: How I'm thinking about different types of automated alignment
entries.summary: The post splits automated alignment into three buckets: empirical research, conceptual research and direct alignment work. It argues the strategic implications differ by bucket.
entries.analysis: Useful framing for oversight and automation strategy.

entries.title: BypassGym: benchmark for AI agents evading endpoint defenses
entries.summary: The paper introduces what it says is the first benchmark testing whether LLM agents can build payloads that evade EDR tools. It fills a gap in offensive-capability evaluations.
